title: Collision can cancel a feature

claims.text:
22. feature-hashing

Target / packet: ai-feature-hashing · D1. Prerequisites: ai:categorical-encoding, cs:hashing-collisions.

Nearest / distinct payoff: categorical-encoding → ai-categorical-encoding. Category encoding allocates explicit identities; a fixed small hash space merges signed token contributions and loses identity.

Finite primary model: Tokens A/B/C counts [1,2,1], declared 2 bucket hash A→0, B→1, C→0. Unsigned vector[2,2]; signs A+, B+, C- give[0,2]. With 3 collision free buckets vector[1,2,1].

Countercase and mathematical boundary: Signed collision may cancel a true coordinate, not recover token identity; counter C count 0 gives signed[1,2]. Fixed hash/sign mappings, no expectation/unbiasedness claim unless proven under stated random family.

Predict and recall transfer: Predict bucket 0 after adding C; recall why hashed vector cannot reconstruct whether A and C canceled.

Required observable evidence: Show each token's bucket/sign contribution and summed vector; no install of hash library.

Source obligation: [scikit-learn feature-hashing documentation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/feature_extraction.htmlfeature-hashing), acquired body §8.2.2. Hash/sign mappings are local and fixed; statistical unbiasedness and collision-frequency claims remain unadmitted.
 Shipped local model and displayed expression addresses: model.ts compute; Demo.tsx Figure; Stage retained computed witnesses.

recall.question: Can bucket 0 equal zero even though A and C both occurred?
recall.why: A contributes +1 and C contributes −1 to the same bucket, summing to zero without removing their occurrences.
